questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people take offence, and the insult 'snowflake'
How snow forms in winter
The history of the book Fight Club
Why free speech should have no limits at all on social media
questions.why: They discuss the new meaning of 'snowflake' as an insult and the complicated topic of offence.

questions.q: Why does Rob act offended at the start?
options: He really is upset with Neil
He dislikes cold weather
He thinks Neil has just called him old and cold
He wants to show what the word means
questions.why: Rob says he wasn't really upset; he just wanted to demonstrate the meaning of the word.

questions.q: Who usually uses the word 'snowflake' as an insult, and about whom?
options: Young people about their parents
People on the left about people on the right
People on the right about young people on the left
Teachers about students
questions.why: Rob says users tend to be from the political right, talking about the left, particularly millennials.

questions.q: According to Rob, what makes offence a difficult subject?
options: Nobody ever means to offend
We don't all find the same things offensive
It only happens on social media, not in real life
It is always about religion
questions.why: He says 'we don't all find the same things offensive'.

questions.q: According to Evan Davis, what do people sometimes do?
options: Say they're offended when it's just a political disagreement
Pretend they are not offended
Refuse to discuss politics
Offend other people by accident without realising they have done it
questions.why: He says people sometimes invoke offence when they really just have a political disagreement.

questions.q: What can groups that suffer discrimination gain from calling it out, according to Davis?
options: Money from the government
More political power and more attention from the media
A feeling of excitement and unity
Protection from the police
questions.why: He says they may find it 'exhilarating or uniting' to call out discrimination.

questions.q: What point does Evan Davis think the so-called snowflakes have?
options: Everyone should be allowed to say anything
Societies can decide some things are taboo
Millennials are wiser than older people
The word 'offensive' should not be used
questions.why: He says 'societies are entitled to make certain things taboo'.

questions.q: What is Rob's own view at the end?
options: Snowflakes should stop complaining
Social media is always a fair place for people to share their views
People should never talk about politics
Free speech is good, but it can be unpleasant
questions.why: Rob says 'Free speech is good but at times, particularly on social media... unnecessarily unpleasant.'
